claims.claim: The deepest hole humans have ever dug
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267, full-text PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf; Zhu & Huang 2026, doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z (full text at nature.com)
claims.note: Lobanov p.268/275: SG-3 reached 12,262 m, 'не превзойдённая до сих пор' (unsurpassed to this day). Zhu & Huang (Feb 2026): 'remains the deepest vertical borehole ever attempted'; the deepest newer wells they list are SDTK-1 10,910 m and X-1 11,156 m. Holds for depth (not length; longer deviated wells exist), and the script never says longest. 'Dug' for drilled is colloquial, not a factual change.

claims.claim: was finished with a bit narrower than a dinner plate
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF (p.276 text, Fig. 5v); Met API https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/201074
claims.note: Lobanov p.276: turbodrill with a 'буровой коронкой диаметром 214 мм' (214 mm core bit); Fig. 5v: open hole d 215.9 mm to 12,262 m. Met object 201074 (acc. 51.86.100), 'Dinner plate', Diameter 25.6 cm. 21.4 cm < 25.6 cm.

claims.claim: Hook as heard by a viewer who swipes away at second two: the deepest hole ever was drilled with a bit narrower than a dinner plate
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF; Zhu & Huang 2026; Met object 201074
claims.note: Literally true as stated: it says the hole was finished with such a bit, not that the hole is that narrow everywhere. (The hole is 72 cm at the top and widened by caverns below 7 km, which the script goes on to say.) A viewer who leaves early takes away nothing false.

claims.claim: The Soviet Union started drilling it in May nineteen seventy
claims.note: Lobanov: 'Бурение было начато 24 мая 1970 г.', a USSR Ministry of Geology project. USGS: 'begun in May, 1970'.

claims.claim: on the Kola Peninsula
claims.note: Lobanov: SG-3 sited in the north-western part of the Kola Peninsula, 10 km west of Zapolyarny (69°25' N, 30°44' E).

claims.claim: At the top, the hole was seventy-two centimetres wide.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF, Fig. 5v (actual well construction), embedded image extracted and read
claims.note: Fig. 5v: 'd 720 мм, 40 м' at the top. Strictly that is the diameter of the top casing column, so the bore there is at least 72 cm; 'seventy-two centimetres wide' is a fair rounding.

claims.claim: It was drilled in steps, each narrower than the last, down to a bit just twenty-one centimetres across.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF Fig. 5v and p.276; USGS OFR 86-517 (Design of the Well; Drill Bits)
claims.note: Fig. 5v steps down: 720 mm to 40 m, 325 mm to 2,000 m, 245 mm to 8,770 m, open hole 215.9 mm to 12,262 m. Bit 214 mm (Lobanov p.276), said as twenty-one. The diameters fall at every step. Caveat: the USGS summary of Kozlovskiy says sections were drilled, then widened with reamers when new casing was needed, so the steps describe the finished hole, not the order things were done in. The wording still holds as a description of the finished hole.

claims.claim: By nineteen seventy-five, it was over seven kilometres deep.
claims.note: 'Первый этап бурения был завершён в мае 1975 г., когда скважина достигла глубины 7 263 м.'

claims.claim: In nineteen seventy-nine, at almost nine point six kilometres, it beat the American record.
claims.note: 'В июне 1979 г. скважина побила рекорд в 9 583 метра, принадлежащий скважине США, достигнув глубины 9 584 метра.' 9.584 km is 'almost nine point six'.

claims.claim: By the end of nineteen eighty-three, it had reached twelve kilometres.
claims.note: '27 декабря 1983 г. глубина скважины достигла 12 000 м.'

claims.claim: Then, in nineteen eighty-four, the drill string broke, and they had to start again from seven kilometres down.
claims.note: '27 сентября 1984 г. бурение СГ-3 было продолжено... на глубине более 12 км произошла авария — оборвалась буровая колонна... Лишь спустя 7 месяцев бурение возобновили заново с глубины 7 000 м.' The third branch was started at 7,010 m off the first.

claims.claim: By nineteen ninety, the new branch had reached twelve thousand, two hundred and sixty-two metres.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF p.275, p.277; Zhu & Huang 2026
claims.note: Lobanov: 'В 1990 г. была достигнута максимальная глубина — 12 262 м'; the third branch, from 7,010 m, 'завершился на 12 262 м'. Zhu & Huang: 'between 1970 and 1989'. 'By 1990' is true on either date.

claims.claim: No hole has gone deeper since.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF p.275, p.281; Zhu & Huang 2026
claims.note: Lobanov 2021: 'не превзойдённая до сих пор'. Zhu & Huang (published 3 Feb 2026): 'remains the deepest vertical borehole ever attempted'. Holds for depth.

claims.claim: The rock at the bottom was expected to be around a hundred and twenty degrees.
claims.note: 'на глубине около 12 км значения температур достигли 212°С, вместо предполагавшихся 120°С.' Celsius (the voice gives no unit; the screen does).

claims.claim: At ten kilometres, it was already a hundred and eighty.
claims.note: Lobanov: 'на глубине 10 км достигла 180°С'. Zhu & Huang: '180 °C at 10 km'.

claims.claim: At the bottom, it was over two hundred.
claims.note: 212 °C at about 12 km (Lobanov), '212 °C at 12 km' (Zhu & Huang).

claims.claim: Below seven kilometres, the walls kept caving in, and the hole went oval, with many caverns.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF p.277-278; USGS OFR 86-517 (Cavity Formation in the Drill Hole)
claims.note: Lobanov: deeper than 7 km 'ствол принял овальную форму, появилось множество каверн, участились аварии'; at more than 7,000 m the bore had an elliptical cross-section; in Archean rocks there were 'обрушениям стенок скважины' (wall collapses). USGS: cavities formed during drilling, the largest at tectonic contacts.

claims.claim: Drilling stopped in nineteen ninety-two, when its funding was cut.
claims.note: Lobanov: 'резкое сокращение финансирования не позволило продолжить работы. Бурение прекратили в 1992 г.' Zhu & Huang blame heat and plastic rock flow instead, in an uncited sentence. The script states only Lobanov's account (A3), and the SOURCES block records the disagreement.

claims.claim: The plan had been to go on to thirteen kilometres.
claims.note: Lobanov p.278: in 1992 a casing string was run 'для продолжения бурения скважины до глубины 13 км'; p.272: the design depth was 15 km, with 13 km to be reached by 1990. In context, the line is about the 1992 plan, so 13 km is right. Zhu & Huang give 15 km as the original goal, so a viewer could raise 15 km, but the line does not say 'original'.

claims.claim: it never made it through the crust: it got about a third of the way.
claims.source_checked: USGS OFR 86-517 https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (p. ii-iii, Results of deep geophysical studies)
claims.note: USGS: 'Crustal thickness in the vicinity of the corehole was shown to be about 40 km'; average Moho on the Kola Peninsula 37 km (28-40). 12.262/40 = 31%, and 12.262/37 = 33%. 'About a third' holds either way.

claims.claim: Twelve kilometres down. The centre of the Earth is over six thousand more.
claims.note: Volumetric mean radius 6,371.000 km (polar 6,356.752). 6,371 - 12.262 = 6,359 km, and even from the polar radius it is over 6,300 km.

claims.claim: DEEPEST HOLE
claims.note: As claim 1.

claims.claim: 21 CM BIT / 8 IN
claims.note: 214 mm bit = 21.4 cm, shown rounded as 21 cm. 21 cm / 2.54 = 8.27 in and 21.4 cm = 8.43 in, both '8 IN'.

claims.claim: MAY 1970
72 CM AT THE TOP / 28 IN
DOWN TO 21 CM / 8 IN
claims.note: 214 mm bit, 215.9 mm open hole: 21 cm (8.3-8.5 in, so '8 IN').

claims.claim: OVER 7 KM / OVER 4.3 MI
claims.note: 7,263 m in May 1975. 7 km = 4.35 mi and 7.263 km = 4.51 mi, so 'over 4.3 mi' is true.

claims.claim: AMERICAN RECORD
claims.note: Record of 9,583 m held by a US well, beaten in June 1979.

claims.claim: 12 KM / 7.5 MI
BACK TO 7 KM / 4.3 MI
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267, full-text PDF https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf, p.277 (text extracted and read); arithmetic; the other km/mi cards in src/shorts/deepest-hole-long/index.tsx
claims.note: Lobanov p.277: after the 27 Sep 1984 string break, 'Лишь спустя 7 месяцев бурение возобновили заново с глубины 7 000 м' (drilling restarted from 7,000 m); the record (third) branch was started at 7,010 m. 'BACK TO 7 KM' says what the source says. 7 / 1.609344 = 4.3496 mi, so '4.3 MI' is right (4.4 would need the 7.01 km figure, 4.356 mi, which the card does not show). Matches the 'OVER 7 KM / OVER 4.3 MI' card; the other cards (12 KM/7.5, 10 KM/6.2, 13 KM/8.1, 6,000+ KM/3,700+) use the same factor. The SOURCES block item 18 still says '7.01 km = 4.36 mi, "4.4 MI"', which no longer describes this card; the card is correct, that line is out of date.

claims.claim: STILL THE DEEPEST
claims.note: As claim 13.

claims.claim: EXPECTED: 120 °C / 248 °F
180 °C AT 10 KM / 356 °F AT 6.2 MI
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF p.280; Zhu & Huang 2026; arithmetic
Lobanov 2021 PDF p.280; Zhu & Huang 2026; arithmetic

claims.claim: WALLS CAVING IN
claims.note: As claim 17 (wall collapses in the Archean section).

claims.claim: 1992: FUNDING CUT
claims.note: As claim 18.

claims.claim: PLAN: 13 KM / 8.1 MI
STILL IN THE CRUST
claims.note: 12.3 km against about 40 km of crust (USGS). Zhu & Huang: 'Despite not penetrating the Moho'.

claims.claim: 12 KM DOWN / 7.5 MI
claims.note: 12.262 km rounded down. 12 km = 7.46 mi.

claims.source_checked: NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet; arithmetic

claims.claim: Plate drawing: photographed dinner plate taken as 25.6 cm across, circles to scale at 21 cm (bit) and 72 cm (top of hole)
claims.source_checked: Met API object 201074 (acc. 51.86.100; additionalImages includes 150793.jpg, the photo used); Lobanov 2021 Fig. 5v and p.276; public/SOURCES.json entry for public/cutout/hole/plate.jpg
claims.note: Met: 'Diameter: 10 1/16 in. (25.6 cm)', and image 150793 is an image of this object. Circles at 21 cm (214 mm bit, about 2% under) and 72 cm (720 mm top). The code scales them from PLATE_CM = 25.6.

claims.claim: Depth/year chart: 12.066 km at 1984.74 (27 Sept 1984), drop to a branch at 7.01 km, restart at 1985.33 at 7.01 km
claims.note: Break during the run resumed on 27 Sept 1984 (1984.74). The second branch's final depth was 12,066 m, the third branch started at 7,010 m, and drilling resumed 7 months later (1985.32). One wrinkle: Lobanov also says 12,066 m was reached 'в 1983 г.' and then drilling was paused, so the dashed join from 12.0 (Dec 1983) to 12.066 (Sept 1984) suggests drilling during the pause. The code's own comment says the joins are not readings, and the slope is about 4 px, so this is not visible.

claims.claim: Depth/year chart: line to 12.262 km at 1990, flat 12.262 km bar from 1989 to 1991
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF p.275, p.277; Zhu & Huang 2026
claims.note: Lobanov: 1990; back near 12 km 'только через 6 лет' after 1984; depth 12,262 m as of 1 May 1991. Zhu & Huang: 1989. The bar spans the sources' disagreement.

claims.claim: Chart axes 0/5/10 KM, 1970/1980/1990, 2/4/6/8 MI; US RECORD line at 9.583 km; PLAN line at 13 km
claims.source_checked: Lobanov 2021 PDF p.274, p.278; src/shorts/deepest-hole-long/index.tsx (read only)
claims.note: US record 9,583 m and 13 km plan, as in claims 9 and 19. Mile ticks are placed at mi × 1.609344 km on the same linear km scale, which is correct.

claims.claim: Thermometer: 0/50/100/150/200 °C against 32/122/212/302/392 °F, expected 120 dashed, mercury rising
claims.note: Each °F tick = °C × 9/5 + 32 (32, 122, 212, 302, 392). 120 expected; mercury to 212.

claims.claim: Caving-walls card: bore with walls breaking outward, labelled NOT TO SCALE
claims.note: Walls breaking outward matches wall collapse and 'значительным изменениям её радиальных размеров' (the hole widening). The not-to-scale label satisfies A6.

claims.claim: Crust card: hole drawn one third of the way through a crust of about 40 km, rest dotted
Centre card: Earth cut open with a line from surface to centre
claims.note: A schematic with no figures; it goes with claim 21.
